Vow of Chastity
VOW uv CHAS-tih-tee
n. (the second monastic vow: perpetual celibacy, sworn for life)
Latin castitas, purity, from castus, pure or chaste; with votum, a vow.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The vow of chastity is sworn lifelong celibacy. Scripture does recognise a genuine gift of singleness, and recognises that it frees a man for undistracted service: “He that is unmarried careth for the things that belong to the Lord, how he may please the Lord” (1Co 7:32), and Christ's own words, “there be eunuchs, which have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven's sake” (Mat 19:12). But the same passages hedge the gift about with cautions a vow cannot honour. “All men cannot receive this saying, save they to whom it is given” (Mat 19:11) makes it a gift, not an undertaking; “every man hath his proper gift of God, one after this manner, and another after that” (1Co 7:7) refuses to rank the two; and Paul's plain provision for the man who finds he lacks the gift is marriage: “if they cannot contain, let them marry: for it is better to marry than to burn” (1Co 7:9). A vow forecloses that remedy for life, on the strength of a young man's estimate of himself. Worse, by elevating celibacy to a higher estate it slanders marriage, which Scripture declares “honourable in all” (Heb 13:4) without qualification.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines chastity as purity of the body, freedom from all unlawful commerce of sexes, and in a single person continence; celibacy as single life, the state of an unmarried person; and marriage as the act of uniting a man and woman for life.

expand to see more

CHASTITY, n. Purity of the body; freedom from all unlawful commerce of sexes. Before marriage, purity from all commerce of sexes; after marriage, fidelity to the marriage bed.

CELIBACY, n. An unmarried state; a single life. It is most frequently applied to the single state of males.

CONTINENCE, n. In a general sense, the restraint which a person imposes upon his desires and passions; chastity.

MARRIAGE, n. The act of uniting a man and woman for life; wedlock; the legal union of a man and woman for life.

HONOURABLE, a. Worthy of honor; illustrious; noble; conferring honor; consistent with honor or reputation.

Key Scripture

1Co 7:32 — "But I would have you without carefulness. He that is unmarried careth for the things that belong to the Lord, how he may please the Lord:"

Mat 19:12 — "For there are some eunuchs, which were so born from their mother's womb: and there are some eunuchs, which were made eunuchs of men: and there be eunuchs, which have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven's sake. He that is able to receive it, let him receive it."

1Co 7:9 — "But if they cannot contain, let them marry: for it is better to marry than to burn."

Heb 13:4 — "Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled: but whoremongers and adulterers God will judge."

Modern Corruption

Sworn lifelong celibacy: a real gift turned into a binding undertaking, and a higher estate invented at the expense of marriage.

expand to see more

The corruption is doctrinal and Paul names it among the gravest. Teaching that forbids marriage he assigns not to zeal but to deception: “in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils” (1Ti 4:1), “Forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats, which God hath created to be received with thanksgiving” (1Ti 4:3). A rule requiring celibacy of all clergy is in exactly that line, and the pastoral wreckage it has produced across centuries is the predictable fruit of binding what God left free. Scripture's own qualification for an overseer assumes the opposite: “A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife” (1Ti 3:2).

The modern misuse runs the other way: a culture that cannot imagine continence at all, and treats the unmarried Christian as deprived by definition. That is its own error. The principle to recover is Paul's balance — singleness is a real gift with real freedom, marriage is honourable in all, neither is a rank, and no man should swear away a remedy God has provided: “not that I may cast a snare upon you” (1Co 7:35).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek hagneia (G47), purity; Greek egkrateia (G1466), self-control; Greek charisma (G5486), a gift of grace; Greek gameo (G1060), to marry; Hebrew tahor (H2889), clean.

expand to see more

Greek hagneia (G47) — purity, chastity; a quality required of every Christian, married or not.

Greek egkrateia (G1466) — self-control; “But if they cannot contain, let them marry” (1Co 7:9) turns on the lack of it.

Greek charisma (G5486) — a gift of grace; “every man hath his proper gift of God” (1Co 7:7).

Greek gameo (G1060) — to marry; “Forbidding to marry” (1Ti 4:3) is what Paul calls a doctrine of devils.

Hebrew tahor (H2889) — clean, pure; purity in Scripture is of the heart first, and of the body as its expression.

Usage

"“All men cannot receive this saying, save they to whom it is given” (Mat 19:11) — a gift, which no vow can confer."

"“Marriage is honourable in all, and the bed undefiled” (Heb 13:4) — the clause that forbids a higher estate."

"“Forbidding to marry” (1Ti 4:3) — the apostolic verdict on a compulsory rule."
